question: What is the primary definition of a research problem in nursing?

options.A: A personal complaint made by a hospital patient
options.B: An administrative rule set by the nursing council
options.C: An area of concern requiring systematic investigation
options.D: A financial deficit within the healthcare facility

explanation: A research problem represents a specific gap in knowledge or clinical difficulty that needs structured study to resolve. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must a research study begin with a clearly defined problem?

options.A: It guarantees immediate funding from international health donors
options.B: It eliminates the need for any statistical data analysis
options.C: It gives direction and guides the entire research process
options.D: It prevents nurses from engaging in bedside clinical duties

explanation: A clear problem statement serves as the compass for the study, shaping methodology, objectives, and data collection. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h1)

question: A ward nurse notices an increase in catheter-associated urinary tract infections despite standard care. What is this observation?

options.A: A disciplinary failure that requires immediate staff suspension
options.B: A practical clinical source for a new research problem
options.C: A normal administrative cost of running a busy hospital ward
options.D: An irrelevant incident that should not be documented or studied

explanation: Recurring clinical issues and negative patient outcomes observed at the bedside serve as prime starting points for nursing research. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h2)

question: Routine patient care observations help identify research topics primarily through what means?

options.A: Noticing gaps or failures in standard nursing interventions
options.B: Reviewing hospital financial balance sheets at month end
options.C: Reading international textbooks published decades ago
options.D: Listening to political debates on national television

explanation: Observing where current bedside care falls short highlights areas that require scientific investigation. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do recommendations in published research articles assist in finding new problems?

options.A: They dictate the exact salary scale for researchers in hospitals
options.B: They provide ready-made answers to clinical exams for nursing students
options.C: They list the names of patients who participated in the study
options.D: They highlight specific knowledge gaps left unaddressed by past authors

explanation: Authors routinely suggest areas where their own studies fell short or where new questions arose, guiding future researchers. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h3)

question: Reading existing nursing literature before starting a study helps primarily to achieve what?

options.A: Reduce the total number of working hours for staff nurses
options.B: Avoid unnecessary duplication of previous research work
options.C: Increase the financial budget allocated to the hospital
options.D: Completely eliminate all forms of human error in surgery

explanation: Literature reviews ensure that researchers do not waste time investigating questions that have already been thoroughly answered. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why are nursing theories considered a valuable source for research problems?

options.A: They reveal discrepancies between theoretical ideals and actual clinical practices
options.B: They automatically cure chronic diseases without the need for medications
options.C: They provide legal protection against medical malpractice lawsuits in court
options.D: They dictate the exact architectural design required for hospital wards

explanation: Testing whether theoretical models hold true in everyday clinical environments generates important research questions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h4)

question: A conceptual framework in nursing research serves what primary purpose?

options.A: It lists all the drugs available in the central pharmacy
options.B: It calculates the monthly wages of nursing department staff
options.C: It organizes ideas and guides the investigation of relationships
options.D: It determines the cleaning schedule for the hospital theater

explanation: Frameworks give researchers a structural lens through which to examine variables and interpret findings. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the benefit of choosing a research problem aligned with national health priorities?

options.A: There will be no need for statistical analysis of the results
options.B: Data collection can be completed in less than twenty-four hours
options.C: The researcher is exempted from obtaining ethical clearance approval
options.D: Findings are more likely to influence health policy and funding

explanation: Government agencies and international bodies prioritize funding and policy changes for research addressing urgent public health goals. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a major national healthcare priority in Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing maternal and child mortality rates
options.C: Studying luxury spa preferences among tourists

explanation: National priorities focus on critical public health concerns rather than commercial leisure activities unrelated to disease burden. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h5)

question: How should a nurse researcher approach a research problem derived from personal experience?

options.A: Publish the findings immediately without peer review or editing
options.B: Assume that all other healthcare workers share the exact same view
options.C: Transition from subjective curiosity to objective scientific inquiry
options.D: Rely entirely on personal opinion without collecting any data

explanation: Personal interest starts the process, but formal research demands objective methodology to ensure valid, unbiased results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h6)

question: Interprofessional friction or communication issues on a hospital ward can lead to what?

options.A: Practical research problems regarding team collaboration and safety
options.B: Zero incidence of medical errors during night shift duties
options.C: Immediate closure of the healthcare institution by the police
options.D: Automatic promotion for junior nursing staff members

explanation: Workplace dynamics and communication challenges directly affect patient safety, making them valid topics for study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h6)

question: What does the feasibility of a research problem primarily refer to?

options.A: Availability of necessary time, money, and study subjects
options.B: The personal popularity of the researcher among colleagues
options.C: The aesthetic design and color of the printed questionnaire
options.D: Whether the final report can be written in poetry format

explanation: Feasibility checks whether a study can realistically be completed given available resources and constraints. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h7)

question: A student proposes a study that requires expensive laboratory equipment the school lacks. Which evaluation criterion fails?
explanation: Lack of required resources like equipment or funding means the study fails the feasibility test and must be modified. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h7)
